decisions.quote:
This investigation replicates and extends an investigation by Wei et al. (
2024
) regarding the effects of prompts-activated purposeful reading, pre-reading expert referent networks (Study 1), and post-reading network-based writing feedback (Study 2) on the quantity and quality of multiple document integration. As expected and consistent with Wei et al. (
2024
), pre-reading integrative prompts improved the quantity of integration in both studies (i.e., η
2
values are around 0.50).
decisions.reason: The replicated component from Wei et al. (2024) is the manipulation of pre-reading prompts (integrative vs. detailed prompts), for which Wei et al. (2024) found a positive effect on integration quantity but not on semantic or structural quality (lines 307-311). Both Study 1 and Study 2 replicate this exact pattern (significant prompt effect on integration quantity and no main effect of prompts on semantic or structural quality; lines 607-703, 870-930, 1031-1032), and the authors explicitly conclude that their investigation agrees with and supports Wei et al. (2024) (Abstract, lines 55-56; General discussion, lines 995-1000; Conclusion, lines 1107-1109). The difference in delayed-writing structural quality (GC_sim) noted in lines 1050-1066 is explicitly attributed by the authors to the new extension intervention—giving all participants an expert referent network before reading or as post-writing feedback, which was not present in Wei et al. (2024) ('Note that participants were not given an expert network in that investigation. This suggests that the expert network, whether given before reading or as writing feedback, influences the conceptual structure of delayed essays')—rather than a failed replication of an original claim.

decisions.quote:
In both Study 1 and Study 2 the essay network structural quality of integration for delayed writing three days later (GC
sim
relative to the expert network) was substantially larger in Session 2 (GC
sim
means range from 0.45 to 0.59) than in Session 1 (GC
sim
means range from 0.20 to 0.25). However, this increase was not observed in Wei et al. (
2024
), where the average GC
sim
values for the delayed writing were 0.23 and 0.24, and for the delayed concept mapping, 0.35 and 0.36.
decisions.reason: While both studies replicate Wei et al.'s (2024) finding that integrative reading prompts improve integration quantity, the authors explicitly contrast the substantial increase in structural quality (GC_sim) at delayed writing with the absence of such an increase in Wei et al. (2024), and no overall verdict on the replication as a whole overrides this stated contrast.
